title: BenchX work order
description: The runner's single input: what to run, at what, how, and for whom (docs/design/runner-schema.md §3). A work order is plain JSON, written by hand, a scheduler, a CI job, or the workbench. The runner reads nothing else.
$comment: Shared primitives ($defs/token, $defs/nonEmptyString, $defs/uri, $defs/sha256, $defs/sourceRef, $defs/parameterValue) are $refs into urn:benchx:schema:measurement-result:0.1.0#/$defs; a validator must register both schemas together (e.g. a referencing.Registry in Python, addSchema in ajv). The `benchmark` field is not in the original runner-schema.md draft: it closes a gap found while planning this schema (see runner-schema.md §3.3) — every non-thin result requires benchmark.source/revision, and nothing in §3's original field table supplied them. `plan` is required exactly when state is resolved (see the allOf below); this schema cannot express the rest of §3.2's resolution rules (a resolved order never differs from what its draft would resolve to; the runner refuses a draft with an unpinned branch name or a versionless policy). A name may not appear in both environment_variables and workload_parameters; the runner enforces this, not the schema. suites[].filter is mutually exclusive with include/exclude; which an adapter supports is its own capability, not a schema promise. The runner never builds: the former `revision` target kind and `build.cache` were removed as unimplemented draft fields, and `build` now only declares the prebuilt target's configuration. The three kinds of target also take the optional provenance text how_built, activation, shell and provider ($defs/provenanceText): declared by the user, recorded as given, never executed or checked. An earlier revision loosened environment_policy from required to optional and widens precision, adding no breaking change, so it stays at 0.1.0.

work_order_id.description: Stable name for this order: a URI or UUID.

project.description: Project in the store. Omit for an ad hoc run; results are then thin (result schema §4.1).

quantities.description: Quantities to collect, e.g. wall-time, peak-rss.

target.description: What code to measure (§3.1): always something already built or present. No kind checks out or builds a revision.

benchmark.description: Where the benchmark suite's own code lives, when different from target (§3.3 addendum). Absent means the benchmarks live in the same checkout as target.

build.description: The declared configuration of the prebuilt target, for facts the runner cannot read from it. Never an instruction to build.

precision.description: Harness-neutral precision settings, spelled per the result schema's Appendix B (comparison_context.protocol.{repetitions,calibration,warmup}).

repetitions.description: How many observations to take. A bare integer is shorthand for one level at unit 'repetition'; the object form supports harnesses that repeat at more than one level (e.g. a process count outside a per-process repetition count).

calibration.description: How the inner iteration count inside one repetition is chosen.

warmup.description: Discarded measurements before the recorded ones. mode distinguishes a count-based warmup (a number of repetitions) from a duration-based one, since harnesses split on this (e.g. Google Benchmark warms up by time only).

schedule.description: Interleaving across sides of a comparison.

environment_policy.description: Named policy (schemas/environment-policy/0.1.0). Optional: absent means the runner applies no policy and only records observed context, the default `benchmark-environments.md`'s laptop scenario describes.

environment_variables.description: Environment variables set for the measured process, on top of the environment the runner inherited. Workload coordinates, not machine facts: each name and value is copied into coordinates.workload.parameters, so a run at OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and one at 10 are different, non-pooling workload variants. Values are strings; one order carries one assignment.

workload_parameters.description: Parameters passed to the runner or the harness, never as environment variables. Copied into coordinates.workload.parameters alongside environment_variables; a name may not appear in both.

run_key.description: Groups this order with sibling orders in one comparison.

round.description: Position in an interleaved run; set by the run author.

reason.description: Free text: why this run exists.

plan.description: Every case x quantity the run will attempt. Required exactly when state is resolved (§3.2, §6). For a harness whose cases are only enumerable from the prebuilt target (e.g. by filter against a compiled binary), the runner fills this in as part of resolving a draft order: it runs the harness's own case-listing step, writes the filled plan into a new resolved order, hashes and records that as the provenance artifact, and only then executes. A hand-authored resolved order (e.g. from a scheduler that already knows the case list) skips that step.

from.description: The suite's include pattern (or filter) this entry was expanded from, when the plan was filled in by the runner rather than hand-authored.

filter.description: Harness-native filter string, passed through unchanged (e.g. a Google Benchmark --benchmark_filter regular expression). An alternative to include/exclude for adapters with only single-pattern, no-exclude selection; mutually exclusive with them.

provenanceText.description: User-owned text about how a target was prepared, declared and recorded as given (benchmark-environments.md §3.2). Never executed and never checked; the runner copies it into provenance.info of every result. Absent, null, empty, or whitespace-only means not declared. None of it enters identity. It is copied verbatim into results that may reach a shared store, so none of it may hold secrets.

how_built.description: What the user did to build the target, such as the cmake commands or the name of the build script.

activation.description: What the user ran to enter the target's environment, such as sourcing an activate script, loading modules, or exporting library paths. The user activates before invoking benchx; the runner records the environment it inherited beside this declaration.

shell.description: The shell the activation text is written for, such as bash: a bare name or an absolute path. Never invoked.

provider.description: Audit-only identity of the target provider that produced the description.

sourceDir.description: Local checkout path to inspect for revision, dirty state, and tree id, when it differs from what the target itself records (e.g. a build directory's own CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY). Optional; falls back to the target's own record when absent.
